original_question: Suppose a Costas array has the property that after adding one blank row at the top, every cyclic shift of the rows still yields a non-square array with the Costas property. Must the original Costas array be an exponential Welch W1 array?
target_in_paper: Section 6.2, Problem 15: the inverse problem asking whether the row-shift property obtained after adjoining one blank row characterizes exponential Welch arrays W_1^{exp}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it has the correct hypothesis (insert one blank row at the top and require every cyclic row shift to preserve the Costas property in the resulting non-square array) and the correct intended conclusion (the original array should be an exponential Welch array). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
missing_details: The paper’s exact target family is the exponential Welch family W_1^{exp}, not the broader Welch family W_1; Theorem 1 gives the precise form: for a prime p, a primitive root α of the finite field F(p), and c∈{0,…,p−2}, the permutation is f:[p−1]→[p−1], f(i)=α^{i-1+c} mod p. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=1112b33e03d236e8189ac3f49b825656fd5198e5&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

To make the question stand-alone, the order of the original array should be named, say n, and the operation should be stated explicitly as producing an (n+1)×n array by inserting one all-zero row above the n×n Costas array. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

The universal quantifier should be explicit: every cyclic row shift means all n+1 cyclic shifts of the rows, equivalently all shifts by t∈{0,…,n} modulo n+1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

Because the shifted object is non-square and no longer a permutation array, the relevant meaning of having the Costas property should be stated directly: all displacement vectors between distinct pairs of dots are distinct. That is the vector formulation underlying Definition 1. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=1112b33e03d236e8189ac3f49b825656fd5198e5&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The conclusion should make explicit the order relation n=p−1, since every W_1^{exp}(p,α,c) array has order p−1 by Theorem 1. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=1112b33e03d236e8189ac3f49b825656fd5198e5&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let A be a Costas array of order n. Form an (n+1)×n dot array B by inserting one blank row above A. Assume that for every t∈{0,…,n}, the array obtained from B by cyclically shifting its rows by t positions still has the Costas property, in the sense that the displacement vectors between any two distinct dots are all distinct. Must A then be an exponential Welch array W_1^{exp}(p,α,c) for some prime p=n+1, some primitive root α of F(p), and some c∈{0,…,p−2}, i.e. the Costas array of the permutation f:[p−1]→[p−1] given by f(i)=α^{i-1+c} mod p? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
justification: This draft is targeting §6.2, Problem 15, not the neighboring single-periodicity Problem 14. The nearby context needed for a fully self-contained version is: Definition 1 for the vector-based meaning of the Costas property, Theorem 1 for the exact construction and notation of W_1^{exp} arrays, and §6.2 for the official inverse-problem formulation. I have not supplied an alternate formulation because the nearby discussion motivates the problem but does not present a formally proved equivalent restatement of Problem 15. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
